notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. git diff 3e3581d rewrites its first paragraph; the sentence that now decides the verdict is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." (with the new exemption "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline"). The change decides nothing here: no run has a call whose argument is a map, struct or keyword list spanning several lines, bound or not, and no run creates an ETS table. Every call takes names or one-line literals (GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: name) in opus-1 line 60, haiku-1 line 93, sonnet-1 line 59; name: __MODULE__ in haiku-2 line 68; GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, path, name: name) in sonnet-2 line 57); opus-1's compiled child list is built under children (lines 172-175) before Supervisor.start_link/2 (line 177), and every moduledoc child list is built under children. Not counted, as in 2026-10-22-c: return tuples (haiku-2 lines 100-101), a map bound to state (sonnet-1 lines 87-92), for comprehensions bound to a name (opus-1 lines 123-128, sonnet-1 lines 121-126, sonnet-2 lines 101-106), and haiku-1's raise ArgumentError, / "..." (lines 177-178), which wraps a string. So all five are clean, as under the old text.

The other changes since 3e3581d are outside this case's list: the new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the reworded do: rule, Before you finish step 1, and the testing.md to ex_unit.md rename and edits. The runs' head is ba24972, and git diff ba24972 HEAD -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty. The nine other listed rules have unchanged text and are graded to the sweeps/2026-10-22-c standard: an if on one boolean condition is clean, unless is a Branch violation; single-letter n is counted under Naming, ts and stamps are not; section-label comments and example labels are not counted under Comments; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict; a start_link/1 with a fixed name and no :name option violates the responsive rule; all counts behind GenServer.call violate Pick the abstraction and Use ETS; a one-step with, or an else that relabels a step's mismatch or holds a no-op clause, violates the with rule; a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted; a run with no with and only raising boot-time calls is not exercised; a case whose `_ ->` covers :empty and an unexpired head in a queue prune (opus-1 line 141, sonnet-2 line 117) is not listed under Match every expected shape, as the 2026-10-22-c baseline-opus-1 grade left the same shape.

Designs. All five keep every count in one GenServer's state behind GenServer.call, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated in all five; opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 say so in their moduledocs ("Checks go through a single process", "State lives in a single GenServer", "All checks go through a single GenServer"). Opus-1 left its 2026-10-22-c PartitionSupervisor design for a single GenServer with count-and-queue entries, so Keep each process behind one module is clean where 2026-10-22-c violated it. Haiku-1 moved to MyApp.RateLimiter; haiku-2 uses the top-level RateLimit with a fixed name. Every run reads its limits file inside init/1: JSON through File.read (opus-1, haiku-2) or File.read! (haiku-1), an Elixir file through Code.eval_file/1 (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). No run uses ETS, so the race check does not apply. Opus-1 compiles an example MyApp.Application; all callers sit in the moduledoc or in comments.

With rule: opus-1 and haiku-2 violate it. Opus-1's load_limits/1 (lines 148-159) has five <- steps and an else whose {:ok, _no_default} and bad_users when is_list(bad_users) clauses relabel the second and fifth steps' mismatches and whose {:error, _} = error -> error is a no-op, the shape 2026-10-22-c counted for its haiku-1. Haiku-2's init/1 (lines 84-87) is a one-step with with no else, which the opening sentence ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`.") decides. Haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no with.

Verification, in scratch copies under the grading scratch folder. Opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted; sonnet-1 fails at line 109 (99 characters), which mix format splits; the only other line over 98 characters is opus-1 line 199, in a comment. All five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. No session ran mix format. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; where :name is accepted (all but haiku-2) a second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50; an injected 61-second-old entry was removed by one :sweep message and the live users kept. Opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 compare ids through to_string/1, so 1 and "1" share a count, as their moduledocs say; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 key by the raw id, so "1" got its own 2 after 1 was exhausted. Haiku-2's init/1 returns {:error, :enoent} from its with for a missing file, which start_link/1 passes back on OTP 29.

All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and empty reads; no session called the Skill tool. Expected reads (processes.md) is unmet in all five, as expected for baseline runs told not to invoke skills.
